newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts Bankgesellschaft Berlin ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts Bankgesellschaft Berlin ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Friday it had downgraded Bankgesellschaft Berlin's (BGB) long-term rating to AA minus from AA, and its individual rating to C from B/C.
The long-term and individual ratings of BGB's subsidiary, Berliner Bank, have also been downgraded to AA minus from AA and to C from B/C respectively, IBCA said in a statement.
The short-term ratings of both banks remain unchanged at A1 plus, the agency said.
"The ratings have been taken off RatingWatch, onto which they were placed on 29 November 1996," IBCA said.
IBCA said the downgradings were a result of the announcement that the group would be making gross loan loss provisions of 2.2 billion marks in its 1996 full year results.
"Such a figure is expected to result in the bank reporting net income of zero for 1996, which will still allow it to pay a maintained dividend," IBCA said.

"To be able to do this, the group will inevitably have to draw on hidden reserves. It is not yet clear to what extent this will impact the bank's capital ratios, although it is likely that they will remain strong by German standards."

The agency said the bulk of the loan loss provisions related to commercial lending in Berliner Bank. While this was viewed as a one-off measure to provide a cleaner structure on which to build, the operating environment, especially in Berlin and the surrounding regions of eastern Germany, remained extremely difficult, with corporate insolvencies continuing to run at record levels.

"At the same time changes in senior management were also announced, with the joint chairmen of BGB stepping down not only from BGB but also from their respective operating subsidiaries," IBCA said. "The appointment of Dr Wolfgang Rupf as sole chairman is a positive move but he faces a considerable challenge in progressing the integration of the disparate corporate cultures within BGB."

"The AAA ratings of Landesbank Berlin, the largest operating entity within BGB, and the MTN programme of BGB Finance (Ireland) Plc are not affected," IBCA said. "These ratings are derived from the support of the State of Berlin via the legal mechanism of Anstaltslast."
